# Mayura

> Mayura is a TypeScript framework for building AI agents, typed tools and durable workflows. It is one npm package, `mayura`: the root import is the core SDK (agents, tools, runtime) and every other part is a subpath such as `mayura/provider-openai` or `mayura/workflows/lifecycle`. The `mayura` CLI creates, runs and operates projects.

Rules that matter when writing Mayura code:

- Import from `mayura` or `mayura/<entry point>`, never from `@mayura/...`.
- Schemas use `z` from `mayura` (it is Zod 4); do not install or import `zod` separately.
- Nothing is allowed by default: grant `model:<adapter id>`, `tool:<tool id>`, `effect:<read|write|host>` and each tool capability in `createRuntime({ permissions: { allow } })`.
- Costs are in micros (1,000,000 = 1 US dollar). A run may spend nothing until `limits.maxCostMicros` is set; model adapters need prices and a per-call `maxCostMicros`.
- Mayura generates the JSON Schemas providers need from Zod schemas; providers accept only strict ones, so use `.nullable()`, not `.optional()`, for fields a model may leave empty.
- Check `result.status` before reading `result.output`; `outcome_unknown` means reconcile, not retry.
- Test offline with `scriptedModel` from `mayura/testing`.

## Get started

- [Introduction](docs/introduction.md): What Mayura is, the ideas behind it, and how its parts fit together.
- [Quickstart](docs/quickstart.md): Create a Mayura project in one command, or add a first agent to your own project and run it offline or on a real model.
- [Installation](docs/installation.md): Requirements, the optional packages each part of Mayura needs, and TypeScript settings.
- [V1.2 release validation status](docs/guides/release-readiness.md): Completed local and CI qualification, experimental surfaces and the checks still required before releasing Mayura V1.2.
- [Using Mayura with AI coding agents](docs/ai-agents.md): Point Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other coding assistants at documentation that matches your installed Mayura version.

## Concepts

- [Agents](docs/concepts/agent.md): Define an agent: instructions, a model, typed tools and typed input and output, checked once and reused for every run.
- [Tools](docs/concepts/tools.md): Define typed tools with defineTool: schemas, effects, capabilities, cost, timeouts, refusals and batches.
- [Runtime](docs/concepts/runtime.md): Create a runtime, submit agents, watch their events, cancel them and read their outcome, costs and evidence.
- [Outcomes and errors](docs/concepts/outcomes.md): Every run ends with one outcome: succeeded, failed, blocked, cancelled or outcome_unknown. What each means and what to do.
- [Permissions](docs/concepts/permissions.md): Explicit allow-lists decide which models, tools, effects and capabilities a run may use. Nothing is allowed by default.
- [Costs and budgets](docs/concepts/costs-and-budgets.md): Cap what a run can spend: costs in micros, per-call ceilings, the run cost limit, tool costs and shared budgets.
- [Workflows](docs/concepts/workflows.md): What a Mayura workflow is, when to use one instead of a single agent run, and which workflow entry point to start with.
- [Framework starters](docs/guides/framework-starters.md): Generate Next.js, Hono, React Router, TanStack Start, SvelteKit or Nuxt notebooks with scoped threads and in-run approvals.
- [Retrieval augmented generation](docs/guides/rag.md): Scoped retrieval tools, durable content-addressed ingestion, vector adapters, citations and bounded reranking.

## Agents and models

- [Model providers](docs/guides/model-providers.md): Connect an agent to OpenAI, Anthropic or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with explicit keys, prices and a per-call cost limit.
- [Model registry](docs/guides/model-registry.md): Name models as provider/model from @mayurajs provider packages, with explicit or catalog prices, a per-call cost bound, safe retries and fallback chains.
- [AI gateways](docs/guides/ai-gateways.md): Registry providers for Vercel, Cloudflare, OpenRouter, Portkey, Helicone and LiteLLM, with explicit credentials and bounded billing.
- [Model routing](docs/guides/model-routing.md): Fail over between model providers with createModelRouter: priority order, a circuit breaker and conservative cost accounting.
- [Streaming](docs/guides/streaming.md): Stream one text field of an agent's answer as the model writes it, with guards on every batch and the final output still checked.
- [Vision: images and PDFs](docs/guides/vision.md): Agents that see: send images and PDFs with an agent's input, return screenshots from tools, and keep media checked, limited and out of logs.
- [Voice](docs/guides/voice.md): Transcribe speech and speak text through voice providers, with explicit prices, a per-call cost bound and voice:<id> permissions.
- [Child agents](docs/guides/child-agents.md): Let one agent call another as a tool, spawn child runs from your code, or race speculative branches, under one shared budget.
- [Agent handoffs](docs/guides/agent-handoffs.md): Transfer a conversation to another agent with one run, one budget and separate target permissions.
- [Skills](docs/guides/skills.md): Give an agent SKILL.md folders of task instructions that it loads only when a task needs them.
- [MCP tools](docs/guides/mcp.md): Wrap one operation of a Model Context Protocol server as a Mayura tool, with the effects, permissions and cost you declare.
- [Terminal](docs/guides/terminal.md): Chat with an agent in the terminal, or turn it into a one-shot command, with a person confirming actions and answering questions.
- [Testing](docs/guides/testing.md): Test agents, tools and provider settings without a network or an API key, using scriptedModel from mayura/testing.

## Workflows

- [Workflow composition](docs/guides/workflow-composition.md): Run a fixed graph of tool calls in-process as an agent, or hand it to another agent as a single tool.
- [Durable workflows](docs/guides/durable-workflows.md): Define and run workflows that survive restarts, wait for people and timers, and never repeat a step whose outcome is unknown.
- [Approvals and human input](docs/guides/approvals-and-human-input.md): Stop a durable workflow until a person approves an exact tool call or answers a typed question, and respond from code, CLI or UI.
- [Sagas and loops](docs/guides/sagas-and-loops.md): Compose durable workflows into sagas that undo finished steps when a later one fails, and into loops that repeat until a condition is met.
- [Webhooks](docs/guides/webhooks.md): Accept signed webhook deliveries, verify their HMAC signature and freshness, and start work exactly once per delivery.
- [Operating workflows](docs/guides/workflow-operations.md): Run durable workflows in production: list and inspect runs, cancel, pause, hold the whole fleet, and ship new definition versions safely.

## Data, safety and extensions

- [Storage](docs/guides/storage.md): Persist durable workflows, memory, budgets and jobs in SQLite, PostgreSQL, libSQL (Turso), MySQL, MongoDB, D1 or DynamoDB; run migrations, and back the store up.
- [Threads](docs/guides/threads.md): Keep a user's conversations with an agent in your store, run each new message as a turn with the conversation so far, and delete them for good.
- [Memory and context](docs/guides/memory-and-context.md): Give agents scoped long-term memory with lexical, semantic and hybrid search, and assemble prompt context within a budget.
- [Fine-grained authorization](docs/guides/authorization.md): Authorize scoped resources with the core policy contract and built-in role-based access control.
- [Guardrails](docs/guides/guardrails.md): Check, redact or block what goes into and comes out of an agent with local guards, processor pipelines and model-backed moderation.
- [Lifecycle hooks](docs/guides/lifecycle-hooks.md): Run your own checks and observers at fixed points of an agent run: before model and tool calls, before output release, and at the end.
- [Artifacts](docs/guides/artifacts.md): Store files your agents produce on local disk or in S3, R2 and other file stores, with verified content, per-tenant isolation, safe downloads, audits and backups.
- [Files](docs/guides/files.md): Store and read files in S3, Cloudflare R2 and other object stores, with versions for safe concurrent writes, per-tenant views and permission-gated file tools for agents.
- [Sandboxes](docs/guides/sandboxes.md): Isolated Linux machines for agents to run commands and handle files in, on Docker or a hosted provider, with no network unless allowed and permission-gated tools.
- [Browsers](docs/guides/browsers.md): Real browsers for agents to read and use web pages in, on the Chrome or Edge installed here or a hosted browser service, kept to the origins you allow, with permission-gated tools.
- [Code Mode](docs/guides/code-mode.md): Run small JavaScript programs, including model-written ones, in a sandbox that can call only the tools you allow.
- [Helpers](docs/guides/helpers.md): Small utilities for configuration, secrets, retries, cancellation, pagination, redacted logging and budgeted concurrency.

## Serve, observe and deploy

- [Server and client](docs/guides/server-and-client.md): Serve agents over authenticated HTTP with mayura/server and mayura/server-node, and call them from browsers or Node with mayura/client.
- [AG-UI adapter](docs/guides/ag-ui.md): Expose scoped run events, stored messages, state snapshots/deltas, durable frontend-tool claims/outboxes and approval interrupts through an AG-UI 1.0 Fetch adapter.
- [Authentication and API keys](docs/guides/authentication.md): Who may call Mayura's server: tokens from identity providers verified with their published keys, and API keys issued and checked on your own storage, each mapped explicitly to what the caller may do.
- [React and UI bindings](docs/guides/react.md): Show live agent runs, workflow progress and human response forms in React, or in any UI framework through headless stores.
- [Copy-in UI components](docs/guides/copy-in-ui.md): Install versioned React source components with reviewed file plans, explicit controls and caller-owned Mayura stores.
- [Observability](docs/guides/observability.md): Watch agent runs through their metadata events, keep run summaries, and export logs, traces and metrics to OpenTelemetry.
- [Operator console](docs/guides/operator-console.md): A built-in web console for operators: health, agents and tools, workflow runs, approvals, human requests, fleet control and migrations.
- [Deployment](docs/guides/deployment.md): Run a Mayura app in production: on containers, Kubernetes, managed platforms, virtual machines, serverless functions or inside an app you already run.

## CLI

- [CLI overview](docs/cli/overview.md): Install and run the mayura command: its commands, readable and JSON output, help, version, exit codes and errors.
- [Create a project](docs/cli/init.md): Create a Mayura project from a starter or a template with mayura init, interactively or with flags, then validate and inspect it.
- [Develop with mayura dev](docs/cli/dev.md): Build and run your project with mayura dev, load .env, and rebuild and restart on every saved change.
- [Serve, worker and migrate](docs/cli/run.md): Run your application in production with mayura serve, mayura worker and mayura migrate, and write the module they load.
- [Deploy with mayura deploy](docs/cli/deploy.md): Write a target's deployment files, plan a release and run it with the tools you already use: Docker, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, or a platform package.
- [Operate a server](docs/cli/operations.md): Inspect and control a running Mayura server from the CLI: health, tools, runs, human requests, workflows and the fleet.

## Integrations: files

- [Mesa files](docs/integrations/filestorage-mesa.md): Store files in a Mesa repository, each write a committed change, with @mayurajs/filestorage-mesa: tokens, rebasing writes, limits and errors.
- [Azure Blob Storage files](docs/integrations/filestorage-azure-blob.md): Store files in an Azure Blob Storage container with @mayurajs/filestorage-azure-blob: Shared Key, Entra ID or SAS, preconditions and errors.
- [AgentFS files](docs/integrations/filestorage-agentfs.md): Store files in AgentFS, Turso's SQLite-backed filesystem for agents, with @mayurajs/filestorage-agentfs: single-writer preconditions and limits.
- [Vercel Blob files](docs/integrations/filestorage-vercel-blob.md): Store files in a private Vercel Blob store with @mayurajs/filestorage-vercel-blob: token, preconditions, CDN-bypassing reads, limits and errors.

- [Cedar authorization](docs/integrations/authz-cedar.md): Local Cedar evaluation with scoped identities, pinned policies and schema, trusted attributes and core audit events.

- [OpenFGA authorization](docs/integrations/authz-openfga.md): Native OpenFGA checks with pinned models, explicit scoped relation mappings and core authorization audit events.
- [Oso authorization](docs/integrations/authz-oso.md): Native Oso Cloud authorization checks with scoped typed identities, explicit credentials, bounded transport and core audit events.
- [Permit.io authorization](docs/integrations/authz-permit.md): Native Permit.io PDP checks with explicit scoped identities, instance keys, environment credentials and core audit events.

- [Firebase Authentication ID tokens](docs/integrations/auth-firebase.md): Accept Firebase Authentication ID tokens on Mayura's server with @mayurajs/auth-firebase: checks, tenants, anonymous users and errors.
- [Google sign-in](docs/integrations/auth-google.md): Accept Google ID tokens on Mayura's server, or sign users in with better-auth, using @mayurajs/auth-google: checks, Workspace domains and errors.
- [Microsoft Entra ID access tokens](docs/integrations/auth-entra.md): Accept Microsoft Entra ID access tokens for your API on Mayura's server with @mayurajs/auth-entra: tenants, app-only tokens and errors.
- [Neon Auth tokens](docs/integrations/auth-neon.md): Accept Neon Auth (Neon's managed better-auth) JWTs on Mayura's server with @mayurajs/auth-neon: checks, banned users, options and errors.
- [Okta access tokens](docs/integrations/auth-okta.md): Accept Okta access tokens from a custom authorization server on Mayura's server with @mayurajs/auth-okta: checks, machines, DPoP and errors.
- [Supabase Auth tokens](docs/integrations/auth-supabase.md): Accept Supabase Auth access tokens on Mayura's server with @mayurajs/auth-supabase: roles, anonymous users, MFA, legacy secrets and errors.
- [WorkOS AuthKit and Connect tokens](docs/integrations/auth-workos.md): Accept WorkOS AuthKit session tokens and Connect access tokens on Mayura's server with @mayurajs/auth-workos: checks, machines and errors.

## Integrations: api key services

- [ReqKey API keys](docs/integrations/km-reqkey.md): Accept API keys issued by ReqKey as Mayura server identities with @mayurajs/km-reqkey: every request validated with ReqKey, no cache, explicit grants.
- [Unkey API keys](docs/integrations/km-unkey.md): Accept API keys issued by Unkey as Mayura server identities with @mayurajs/km-unkey: every request verified with Unkey, no cache, explicit grants.

## Integrations: deploy targets

- [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore deploy target](docs/integrations/deploy-agentcore.md): Deploy a Mayura agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime with @mayurajs/deploy-agentcore: an ARM64 image serving its HTTP contract.
- [Amazon ECS deploy target](docs/integrations/deploy-aws-ecs.md): Deploy a Mayura app to Amazon ECS on Fargate with @mayurajs/deploy-aws-ecs: task definitions, a checked migration task, then the services.
- [AWS Lambda deploy target](docs/integrations/deploy-aws-lambda.md): Deploy a Mayura app to AWS Lambda with @mayurajs/deploy-aws-lambda: one container image, a checked migration, then the API and workflows.
- [Azure Container Apps deploy target](docs/integrations/deploy-azure.md): Deploy a Mayura app to Azure Container Apps with @mayurajs/deploy-azure: a migration job run to success, then the server and worker apps.
- [Cloudflare deploy target](docs/integrations/deploy-cloudflare.md): Deploy a Mayura app to Cloudflare with @mayurajs/deploy-cloudflare: the app in Containers, or the serverless module on Workers.
- [DigitalOcean App Platform deploy target](docs/integrations/deploy-digitalocean.md): Deploy a Mayura app to DigitalOcean App Platform with @mayurajs/deploy-digitalocean: server, worker, pre-deploy migration and PostgreSQL.
- [Fly.io deploy target](docs/integrations/deploy-fly.md): Deploy a Mayura app to Fly.io with @mayurajs/deploy-fly: fly.toml, server and worker process groups, the migration as release command.
- [Google Cloud Run deploy target](docs/integrations/deploy-cloudrun.md): Deploy a Mayura app to Google Cloud Run with @mayurajs/deploy-cloudrun: a migration job, then the server and an always-on worker.
- [Railway deploy target](docs/integrations/deploy-railway.md): Deploy a Mayura app to Railway with @mayurajs/deploy-railway: server and worker services from config-as-code files, each migrating first.
- [Render deploy target](docs/integrations/deploy-render.md): Deploy a Mayura app to Render with @mayurajs/deploy-render: a Blueprint with a web service, a background worker and PostgreSQL.
- [Vercel deploy target](docs/integrations/deploy-vercel.md): Deploy a Mayura app to Vercel Functions with @mayurajs/deploy-vercel: the API, workflows advanced by Vercel Cron, storage migrated first.

## Reference

- [Entry points](docs/reference/entry-points.md): Every public entry point of the mayura package: what it is for, its key exports and the optional packages it needs.
- [Integration packages](docs/reference/integrations.md): Every @mayurajs package: model providers, voice, storage, files, observability, sandboxes, browsers, authorization, sign-in, API keys and deploy targets.

- [What's new in Mayura 1.1](docs/project/whats-new.md): Mayura 1.1: a model registry, voice, files, sandboxes, browsers, authentication and API keys, mayura deploy, edge runtimes and 85 integration packages.
- [Versioning](docs/project/versioning.md): What Mayura keeps stable, how versions follow SemVer, how APIs are deprecated, and how release candidates and npm tags work.
- [Support](docs/project/support.md): Supported Node.js versions, platforms and package managers, how to get help with Mayura, and how to report a bug.
- [Security](docs/project/security.md): Mayura's security model: what it protects, what your code is trusted with, and how to report a vulnerability.
- [Credits](docs/project/credits.md): The open-source projects and open standards Mayura is built on, what each one does in Mayura, and its license.
